Boston College Eagles.status: Transfer — from Saginaw Valley State (Division II); described as the early leader rather than a settled starter.
Boston College Eagles.career_experience: Had no FBS offers out of high school; billed as a dual threat with nearly 6,000 total yards and close to 50 touchdowns at Division II level.
Boston College Eagles.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Boston College Eagles.passing: Included in nearly 6,000 total yards and close to 50 touchdowns at Saginaw Valley State; the guide does not split passing out.
Boston College Eagles.rushing: Included in the same combined totals; billed as a dual threat.
Boston College Eagles.competition: Open, with McKenzie only the early leader. Grayson Wilson drew multiple FBS offers and enrolled at Arkansas without playing, so the guide says he starts with a clean slate; freshman Femi Babalola had several Division I offers and the guide says he may be the best long-term option.
Boston College Eagles.backup: Grayson Wilson (Arkansas, never played) and freshman Femi Babalola.
Boston College Eagles.author_confidence: Very low. The guide notes O'Brien enters with virtually no Division I experience at quarterback and frames the step up from Division II as serious.
Boston College Eagles.positive_case: Bill O'Brien has spent much of his career with quarterbacks and the guide says that must be his focus; McKenzie brings dual-threat production, and Babalola may be the best long-term answer.
Boston College Eagles.concerns: A serious step up from Division II for the leader, no Division I experience anywhere in the room, and almost no returning skill production around whoever plays.
Boston College Eagles.scheme_fit: O'Brien is serving as his own coordinator.
Boston College Eagles.supporting_cast: Almost nothing returns. Leading receiver Lewis Bond (88 catches, 993 yards) is gone along with the next two, leaving tight end Kaelan Chudzinski as the top returnee; the top two rushers, who produced 13 touchdowns and over 1,100 yards, have also left. The guide expects Liberty transfer Evan Dickens — 1,339 rushing yards at Liberty — and sophomore Bo MacCormack to help in the passing game given unproven receivers.
Boston College Eagles.portal_context: McKenzie from Saginaw Valley State, Wilson from Arkansas and Dickens from Liberty are the named additions in a wholesale overhaul the guide says a 2-10 team needed anyway.
Boston College Eagles.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 3.5 wins. The only clear favorite role is at home against Maine in Week 3, and the guide's conclusion is about bet construction as much as the team: a likely poor start makes this the wrong sort of team and schedule to chase with. Projection is 3.42 wins.
Boston College Eagles.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide's opening judgement is that finding a quarterback must be O'Brien's focus, and the position has no established answer.

California Golden Bears.status: Returning starter — the guide frames the coaching change as not a total teardown precisely because he is in place.
California Golden Bears.previous_school: Not applicable as a 2026 move — originally committed to Oregon before transferring to Cal ahead of his freshman year.
California Golden Bears.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
California Golden Bears.passing: Over 3,400 yards with an 18-to-9 touchdown-to-interception ratio and 64.2% completions as a true freshman.
California Golden Bears.competition: None described — Sagapolutele is the settled starter.
California Golden Bears.author_confidence: Positive. The guide expects him to grow and concludes he could have a monster season.
California Golden Bears.positive_case: Strong true-freshman production, plus support from former NFL receiver Ike Hilliard on staff, a 1,000-yard Ohio transfer at running back, a big-bodied receiver addition and considerable starting experience on the line.
California Golden Bears.concerns: A new scheme and new receivers — Jacob De Jesus and Trond Grizzell took 163 catches and over 1,800 yards elsewhere.
California Golden Bears.scheme_fit: New and unproven. The guide puts the onus on coordinator Jordan Somerville and Hilliard to find explosiveness, noting Somerville is only 30, with a single year as an Oregon offensive assistant in 2022 enough for Lupoi to want him again.
California Golden Bears.supporting_cast: Rebuilt but credible: 1,000-yard Ohio transfer Chase Henderson, big-bodied Rutgers transfer Ian Strong, and considerable starting experience on the offensive line.
California Golden Bears.portal_context: Chase Henderson from Ohio and Ian Strong from Rutgers arrive; De Jesus and Grizzell departed.
California Golden Bears.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins. The guide separates quality from wins deliberately: Cal may not match last season's seven wins yet has a very good chance of being a much more aesthetically pleasing team. It sets against Sagapolutele's expected growth a completely new staff, no bye until early November, and inevitable growing pains. Projection is 5.74 wins.
California Golden Bears.outlook_dependency: High on quality, low on wins. The guide expects the quarterback to improve while explicitly not expecting that to convert into more victories.
California Golden Bears.conflicts: The guide prints total 11 returning starters with offense 8 and defense 6 on p. 82; offense plus defense is 14, which does not equal the printed total. All three figures are reproduced as printed in the Team Database and none is corrected here.

Clemson Tigers.status: New starter — replacing three-year starter Cade Klubnik.
Clemson Tigers.career_experience: A top-10 quarterback in the 2023 class per 247; light on experience with 105 career attempts.
Clemson Tigers.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide records 105 career attempts.
Clemson Tigers.passing: Not addressed in guide beyond the 105 career attempts.
Clemson Tigers.competition: None described — Vizzina is presented as the starter.
Clemson Tigers.author_confidence: Positive on circumstance rather than on demonstrated production. The guide's conclusion is that even with Vizzina light on experience, Morris's return and a new voice in the huddle will probably help.
Clemson Tigers.positive_case: A top-10 recruit in his class inheriting an excellent receiver room, with the guide arguing it should not take much for the offense to improve given Swinney's talent pipeline.
Clemson Tigers.concerns: Very limited experience — 105 career attempts — while stepping into a programme under scrutiny.
Clemson Tigers.scheme_fit: The guide's central argument is relational: Swinney should be relieved to have coordinator Chad Morris back, his coordinator from 2011 to 2014, because he and Riley were oil and water — which the guide links to how Klubnik's Clemson career ended.
Clemson Tigers.supporting_cast: Excellent receiver room; the backfield is open after Adam Randall's departure, with candidates Chris Johnson, who averaged over seven yards per carry at SMU, and Gideon Davidson, a four-star and top-five back in the 2025 class per 247. Clemson ran for just 3.9 yards per carry last year, down sharply from 5.1.
Clemson Tigers.portal_context: Chris Johnson arrives from SMU; the guide notes Clemson has been under scrutiny for being slow to adapt to the modern landscape and the portal.
Clemson Tigers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, with the LSU opener expected to reveal a lot quickly. The defense was extremely good and the guide says it should not take much for the offense to improve. It flags a futures angle explicitly: Clemson is worth a look at 14-1 to win the ACC. Projection is 7.88 wins.
Clemson Tigers.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's Over depends on offensive improvement from a quarterback with 105 career attempts, and it notes separately that Vizzina must grow into the starting role.

Duke Blue Devils.status: Transfer — from San Jose State; the third straight season Manny Diaz has had to find a quarterback in the portal.
Duke Blue Devils.career_experience: Played extensively at San Jose State.
Duke Blue Devils.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Duke Blue Devils.passing: Over 5,500 yards but only 30 touchdowns against 19 interceptions at San Jose State.
Duke Blue Devils.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate.
Duke Blue Devils.turnovers: 19 interceptions against 30 touchdowns — the ratio the guide sets against Mensah's 34-to-6.
Duke Blue Devils.competition: Live. The guide raises redshirt freshman Dan Mahan as a live alternative, since he took all the spring opportunities available while Eget was hurt.
Duke Blue Devils.author_confidence: Low. The guide sets Eget's 30-to-19 ratio directly against Darian Mensah's 34-to-6 and raises a redshirt freshman as a live alternative.
Duke Blue Devils.positive_case: Extensive playing experience with over 5,500 yards.
Duke Blue Devils.concerns: A poor touchdown-to-interception ratio replacing a quarterback who completed over two-thirds of his passes for nearly 4,000 yards and led the conference in attempts, yards and touchdowns; plus an injury that cost him spring reps.
Duke Blue Devils.scheme_fit: Coordinator Jonathan Brewer improved the group by a full yard per play and 8.3 points per game in year two, but the guide notes he is mostly starting from scratch in year three.
Duke Blue Devils.supporting_cast: Strong on the ground, thin outside. Nate Sheppard ran for 1,132 yards and 11 touchdowns at 5.7 per carry as a true freshman and Duke remains big and experienced up front despite losing an NFL-caliber lineman. The receiving picture is thinner: Penn's 1,000-yard receiver Jared Richardson is an intriguing transfer, but the other two primary targets look like 5-foot-8 Jayden Moore and 5-foot-9 Charlotte transfer Javen Nicholas.
Duke Blue Devils.portal_context: Eget from San Jose State, Richardson from Penn, Nicholas from Charlotte. The guide's framing is structural: portal poaching is hard for mid-tier Power Four schools to overcome annually, and it wonders whether this is the season it hits hard.
Duke Blue Devils.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, with the guide stating the tension in its own view openly by giving a projection of 5.94 wins alongside the Under. It suggests a ground-and-pound approach early and draws the betting implication that this could create value on Unders.
Duke Blue Devils.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's own inference is that Duke was fortunate Mensah played as well as he did, having been comfortably outgained per play in ACC games — which makes the quarterback downgrade central.

Florida State Seminoles.status: Transfer — via Auburn, having previously been at Stanford.
Florida State Seminoles.career_experience: Flashed at Stanford but started only three games at Auburn.
Florida State Seminoles.competition: Not described as live; the guide names redshirt freshman Kevin Sperry alongside him.
Florida State Seminoles.author_confidence: Low, and stated bluntly. The guide says Daniels and Sperry are not the quarterbacks a programme like Florida State should have — and adds that neither was Tommy Castellanos.
Florida State Seminoles.positive_case: He flashed at Stanford, and the surrounding talent is real: Duce Robinson, once the nation's No. 1 tight end recruit, broke out with 56 catches for 1,081 yards; freshman Micahi Danzy averaged over 21 yards per reception; Ousmane Kromah managed 5.7 yards per carry and Samuel Singleton over seven.
Florida State Seminoles.concerns: Only three starts at Auburn, and the guide's blunt conclusion that the position is below the programme's standard — which it links to finance, saying Norvell's buyout appears to hold the programme hostage.
Florida State Seminoles.supporting_cast: Better than the quarterback. Most of last season's skill production came with Castellanos, who led the team in rushing with only 557 yards and posted a 15-to-9 ratio.
Florida State Seminoles.portal_context: Daniels arrives via Auburn; Castellanos has departed.
Florida State Seminoles.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins, though the guide explicitly says this is not a bet — the vig is cost-prohibitive and Florida State projects to have a good defense. Its reasoning is asymmetric rather than pessimistic: even an average quarterback could produce 7-5, but the floor is lower than the ceiling is high. Projection is 6.35 wins.
Florida State Seminoles.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide's entire asymmetry argument is stated in quarterback terms — an average quarterback produces 7-5, and the floor is low because it doubts it has one.

Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.status: Transfer — from Indiana; younger brother of Fernando Mendoza.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.career_experience: Played little at Indiana, since Curt Cignetti rarely eased off.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.competition: None described — Mendoza is presented as the starter.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.author_confidence: Explicitly unknown. The guide is candid that nobody knows what to expect from him.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.positive_case: The staff has succeeded with a portal quarterback before, in Texas A&M transfer Haynes King, and went back to the portal for Mendoza.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.concerns: He played little at Indiana, so there is no body of evidence — and he arrives into wholesale turnover elsewhere.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.scheme_fit: New offensive coordinator George Godsey played quarterback at Georgia Tech from 1998 to 2001 and returns after four seasons as the Ravens' tight ends coach — a fit the guide likes given two of Tech's best portal additions were tight ends. It predicts a more ball-control offense, since Georgia Tech ranked 97th in average time of possession.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.supporting_cast: Almost entirely new. Only one player with at least six receptions returns across the receiver and tight end rooms; Michigan transfer Justice Haynes looks the starter at running back ahead of Malachi Hosley, the most productive returning skill player even though Haynes King led the team in rushing yards and touchdowns; three offensive line starters and the line coach are gone. The guide's summary is deliberately cumulative and it calls this a lot.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.portal_context: Mendoza from Indiana, Justice Haynes from Michigan, plus two productive transfer tight ends. Coordinator Buster Faulkner left for Florida and Blake Gideon returned to Texas.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins, despite a schedule the guide calls unkind late — the year ends with Virginia Tech, Pitt, Louisville, Clemson, Wake Forest and Georgia. Its case rests on three things it names together: what Key has done so far, the caliber of coordinators he has hired, and the programme's portal success. Projection is 6.02 wins.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.outlook_dependency: High but diffuse. The quarterback is one element of a wholesale turnover the guide backs the coaching staff to manage, rather than the single stated hinge.

Louisville Cardinals.career_experience: A multi-sport star from South Dakota who threw only 36 passes in three seasons at Columbus.
Louisville Cardinals.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide; the guide records 36 career passes.
Louisville Cardinals.passing: 36 passes in three seasons at Ohio State.
Louisville Cardinals.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide names his running as a key to the offense.
Louisville Cardinals.competition: Not described as live, but the guide names a more experienced alternative in two-year West Georgia starter Davin Wydner.
Louisville Cardinals.backup: Davin Wydner, a two-year West Georgia starter.
Louisville Cardinals.author_confidence: Positive on talent, silent on evidence. The guide judges the talent should be there and calls getting the position right a huge start.
Louisville Cardinals.positive_case: The talent should be there, and the guide notes Brohm always makes the passing game work.
Louisville Cardinals.concerns: Only 36 career passes, following a predecessor who was not the answer — Miller Moss posted pedestrian numbers with under 3,000 yards and 16 touchdown passes, though the guide notes both he and Tyler Shough at least arrived with substantial college experience, which Kienholz does not.
Louisville Cardinals.scheme_fit: Not addressed directly; the guide's confidence attaches to Brohm's record with passing games.
Louisville Cardinals.supporting_cast: Strong in the backfield, empty outside. Isaac and Keyjuan Brown, unrelated, combined for just under 1,600 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns — Isaac did not match his 1,173-yard freshman season but missed several games at 8.8 yards per carry, and Keyjuan averaged over seven. Against that, Chris Bell and Caullin Lacy accounted for 132 of the team's 268 receptions and over 54% of its receiving yards and are both gone, making Kienholz's running plus the two Browns the keys to offsetting an entirely new receiver corps.
Louisville Cardinals.portal_context: Kienholz from Ohio State and Wydner from West Georgia; Bell and Lacy departed.
Louisville Cardinals.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 8.5 wins. The conference schedule misses Miami and Clemson, and the games against SMU and Pitt are at home. The guide's case is that Brohm always makes the passing game work and this could be his first 200-yards-per-game rushing attack, with the conditional stated precisely: cutting the trademark losses from two to one gets this home at a nice plus-money price, even though its own projection is 8.02 wins.
Louisville Cardinals.outlook_dependency: High. The guide calls getting the quarterback position right a huge start, and its Over depends on the offense functioning with an entirely new receiver corps.

Miami Hurricanes.status: Transfer — from Duke, replacing Carson Beck.
Miami Hurricanes.career_experience: A strong Tulane season followed by a season at Duke; the guide says he has been extremely well coached throughout.
Miami Hurricanes.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Miami Hurricanes.passing: A 34-to-6 touchdown-to-interception ratio at Duke, where he completed over two-thirds of his passes for nearly 4,000 yards and led the conference in attempts, yards and touchdowns.
Miami Hurricanes.turnovers: Six interceptions against 34 touchdown passes at Duke.
Miami Hurricanes.competition: None described — Mensah is the expected starter.
Miami Hurricanes.author_confidence: High. The guide calls him an objectively more talented quarterback than Carson Beck, who himself was excellent, and rates the situation excellent.
Miami Hurricanes.positive_case: A 34-to-6 ratio at Duke after a strong Tulane season, extremely well coached throughout, joining an offense the guide says looks loaded.
Miami Hurricanes.concerns: Not addressed as a quarterback concern; the guide's doubts are about Cristobal's record as a big favorite and about defensive attrition.
Miami Hurricanes.scheme_fit: The guide asks whether Shannon Dawson's offense has another gear with a more talented quarterback, and notes Dawson impressed in the playoff.
Miami Hurricanes.supporting_cast: Excellent. Mark Fletcher and the backfield are all back, and 1,200-yard receiver Malachi Toney leads a rebuilt group that adds Mensah's Duke teammate Cooper Barkate and his own 1,100 yards.
Miami Hurricanes.portal_context: Mensah and Cooper Barkate both arrive from Duke.
Miami Hurricanes.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 10.5 wins. Road games at Clemson and Notre Dame stand out precisely because of Cristobal's habit of losing as a big favorite, and a mechanical point about the market is made: season win total wagers exclude conference title games and the playoff, so dropping either road game would require running the table otherwise. The guide expects Miami in both the title game and playoff and calls this an excellent team on paper while still not recommending the Over. Projection is 10.62 wins.
Miami Hurricanes.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The quarterback is treated as an upgrade and a strength; the Under is argued from Cristobal's favorite-role record and the mechanics of the win-total market.

NC State Wolfpack.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
NC State Wolfpack.passing: Over 3,100 passing yards as part of 31 total touchdowns.
NC State Wolfpack.rushing: 215 rushing yards, included in the 31 total touchdowns.
NC State Wolfpack.competition: None described — Bailey is the settled starter.
NC State Wolfpack.backup: Coastal Carolina transfer Tad Hudson. Backup Will Wilson remains as a short-yardage runner with 10 touchdowns but only five pass attempts.
NC State Wolfpack.author_confidence: Neutral on the quarterback, concerned about everything around him. The guide's audit focuses on departures rather than on Bailey's ability.
NC State Wolfpack.positive_case: 31 total touchdowns with over 3,100 passing yards and 215 rushing.
NC State Wolfpack.concerns: He has lost his top five receivers and leading rusher Hollywood Smothers, who averaged 5.9 yards per carry.
NC State Wolfpack.supporting_cast: Rebuilt from a committee. The guide describes the previous receiving picture as genuinely distributed rather than empty — nobody exceeded 629 yards, but four players had 430 or more and seven had at least 37 catches. Top returnee Keenan Jackson started 13 games for only 28 catches and 281 yards, so the guide looks to Buffalo transfer Victor Snow, Miami transfer Joshisa Trader and holdover back Jayden Scott to stand out rather than repeat the committee approach.
NC State Wolfpack.portal_context: Victor Snow from Buffalo, Joshisa Trader from Miami and Tad Hudson from Coastal Carolina arrive.
NC State Wolfpack.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, with the schedule the primary reason to buy in — the trip to Stanford follows a bye and Cal travels across the country the next week; Vanderbilt away is tough while App State at home is winnable. A specific futures construction is offered: NC State at 22-1 to win the ACC is called a worse-than-average bet to avoid. Projection is 7.09 wins.
NC State Wolfpack.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Over rests on schedule and a high programme floor rather than on quarterback improvement.
